::: {#exm-string}
#### Building a string of DNA bases

Let $\Sigma = \cb{\mathtt{A}, \mathtt{C}, \mathtt{G}, \mathtt{T}}$.
The string $\mathtt{GAT}$ is in $\Sigma^*$ (@def-string), by three applications of the recursive rule:

- $\lambda \in \Sigma^*$ and $\mathtt{G} \in \Sigma$, so $\lambda \mathtt{G} = \mathtt{G}$ is in $\Sigma^*$;
- $\mathtt{G} \in \Sigma^*$ and $\mathtt{A} \in \Sigma$, so $\mathtt{GA} \in \Sigma^*$;
- $\mathtt{GA} \in \Sigma^*$ and $\mathtt{T} \in \Sigma$, so $\mathtt{GAT} \in \Sigma^*$.

The string $\mathtt{GAU}$ is not in $\Sigma^*$,
since the rule adds only symbols of $\Sigma$, and $\mathtt{U} \notin \Sigma$.

:::
